test_setup.clip_construction_method: create_clip (session slot) + add_notes_to_clip, then duplicate_clip_to_arrangement(destination_bar=1) -- create_arrangement_midi_clip's own empty clip could not take notes via add_notes_to_clip (it addresses session clip slots only; errored 'No clip in slot' when tried directly on the arrangement clip).
test_setup.export_method: File > Export Audio/Video, Rendered Track = the specific track (isolates one track from the master mix), Render Start 1.1.1, Render Length 4.0.0, WAV 24-bit 48000 Hz
test_setup.wav_analysis_method: Read WAV via Python wave module, decode 24-bit PCM to float64, compute peak abs value, RMS, and count of non-zero samples across both channels.

test_1_stock_instrument.track: 8-Operator (MIDI track created with create_midi_track, Operator loaded via load_instrument_or_effect uri='query:Synths#Operator')

test_2_serum_arrangement.track: BULK_01_WAVETABLE_MAIN (MIDI track created with create_serum_track, loading BULKCAUSAL_VERIFY/BULK_01_WAVETABLE_MAIN.SerumPreset -- osc B, C, Noise, Sub all enabled per describe_preset)

test_3_serum_after_enable_device.hypothesis_tested: Serum 2 device on the track is bypassed/disabled, silencing the render.
test_3_serum_after_enable_device.action_taken: enable_device(track_index=6, device_index=1) -- returned 'Serum 2 enabled' (does not distinguish 'was already enabled' from 'just enabled').
test_3_serum_after_enable_device.conclusion: Device-enabled/bypass state is RULED OUT as the cause.

diagnosis_summary.confirmed: The Ableton Arrangement export/render mechanism itself is not broken in general -- an equivalent MIDI track + arrangement clip + per-track export using Ableton's own stock Operator instrument produces full, expected audio (peak ~0.40, RMS ~0.15, 100% non-zero samples) under the exact same tempo/clip/export procedure. The silence is specific to tracks created via create_serum_track / Serum 2, not a general Arrangement-export defect. This reproduces the prior project history's finding of digital silence on Serum Arrangement renders.
ruled_out: Serum 2 device bypass/disabled state (tested directly via enable_device, no change)
not_yet_tested_open_hypotheses: Track record-arm state: the working Operator track was armed (arm=true) at creation; the silent Serum tracks are unarmed (arm=false). Whether record-arm affects Ableton's per-track Export rendering (as opposed to normal playback, where arm should not matter) was identified as worth testing but not completed in this session -- locating the Session-view mixer arm button for the Serum tracks required scrolling/resizing the Ableton window in a way that repeatedly proved unreliable via UI automation in this environment (see note below).

Track audio output routing (Audio To): not independently confirmed as 'Master' for the Serum tracks vs the working Operator track -- no AbletonMCP tool exposes track output routing directly; would require UI inspection.

MIDI routing/track input monitoring state specific to how create_serum_track wires the track (its own docstring notes 'no state readback yet' on preset load -- the same may be true of the track's other mixer/routing defaults).

Whether the same Serum track produces audio during ordinary Session-view clip playback (not Arrangement, not export) -- would isolate whether this is an Arrangement-specific or completely general MIDI-to-Serum delivery failure.
diagnosis_summary.environment_note: UI automation in this session showed the Ableton/Serum window position and layout shifting unpredictably between the interactive computer-use automation channel and a separate PowerShell-driven screen-capture channel (see W1/blocker notes on the VLM tooltip capture) -- full mixer-strip inspection (arm/routing buttons) was not completed for this reason, not because it is inherently unavailable.
diagnosis_summary.not_claimed: This diagnosis does NOT claim a root cause. It confirms the symptom is real, reproducible, and isolated to Serum tracks (not a general render-path failure), and rules out one specific hypothesis (device bypass). Root-causing the remaining hypotheses (arm state, output routing, create_serum_track's track-setup defaults) is the recommended next step, ideally with direct AbletonMCP routing/arm tools rather than fragile UI automation.
